Short answer: Choose Airtable when structured records are the center, Notion when shared notes and knowledge are the center, and monday.com when assigned work and status are the center.

What this means for your business

All three can imitate each other. That does not make them equally comfortable. Pick the tool your staff can update during a busy day, not the one with the prettiest demo.

What to watch

  • The same fact copied into several tools.
  • A setup that only one person understands.
  • Guests, automations, storage, or permissions pushing the bill upward.
  • A dashboard that looks busy but changes no decision.

Do this next

  1. Write the one job the tool must own.
  2. Test that job with ten real records and two real users.
  3. Price the plan you will need after the trial, not the free-plan fantasy.
  4. Keep an export and name who owns the account.

When Little Fight fits

We help map the workflow, connect what should stay, and build only when the rented tools make the work worse. If a shared checklist solves it, use the checklist.
